title: Every cited source is emitted as {title, href, kind, context} — no observation time, no freshness verdict, no source-vs-inference distinction, no governed deep link
why_open: The answer path is real and wired, and it cites nothing that can be checked. apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:271-276 maps the six surviving docs to `sources` as exactly { title, href, kind, context }, and apps/web/src/lib/ai.ts:171-176 builds the prompt's sourceBlock from `scored.map(modelSourceFor)` and instructs the model to 'Cite every claim with its source number in brackets'. Neither carries an observation time, a staleness verdict, or any statement of whether a numbered source is a retrieved Tenure record or the model's own inference. SearchDoc itself has no such field — apps/web/src/lib/search.ts:9-30 is { id, kind, title, body, href, context, mode } — and the five construction sites in apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:123-134 (memory), :146-155 (document), :170-181 (approval), :187-195 (event), :200-208 (organization) never select `updatedAt` at all: the four Prisma selects at search-data.ts:72, :78-84, :88-95, :99 and the org select at :58 contain no timestamp column. The second consumer, apps/web/src/app/api/search/route.ts:22-28, is the same shape. Bible §3.5 (line 241 of the Bible) says 'Never answer as though a stale, deleted, inaccessible, or reconciliation-failed source is current. Show freshness and uncertainty', and §9.3 (line 591) requires 'source provider, object title/type..., event/version time, last sync time, and a governed deep link' plus 'The user can distinguish source text, Tenure record, Relay inference, and human-approved memory'. Grep for freshness/observedAt/citation across apps/web/src and packages/*/src finds only packages/finops/src/reporting.ts (a cost-report Freshness type, in a package this run may not touch) and the word 'citation' in a comment at search.ts. The ledger has WRK-070-003 FAIL at docs/implementation/universal-work-graph-execution-ledger.md:527-529 and that is correct.
smallest_real_change: Copy the shape WRK-010-003 already proved in this exact file: `mode: ProjectionMode` was added to SearchDoc as a REQUIRED field so tsc enumerated every construction site (search.ts:16-29 says so in its own comment). Do the same with a required `citation`. (1) apps/web/src/lib/relay/citation.ts — sibling of the existing relay/projection-policy.ts, kernel-free so tests can import it directly: `SourceCitation` = { origin: 'TENURE_RECORD' | 'EXTERNAL_PROJECTION', assertion: 'SOURCE' | 'INFERENCE', observedAt: string, state: ProjectionState, deepLink: string | null } and `freshnessOf(observedAt, now, staleAfterMs)` returning CURRENT | STALE per §3.5, plus `governedDeepLink(providerId, url)` which returns null unless the provider is activated (providerActivation from @tenure/platform-config, the same gate api/ai/chat/route.ts:298-302 already calls) AND the URL's origin matches that provider's declared host — never the raw stored URL. (2) Widen SearchDoc with required `citation: SourceCitation`; the ONLY construction sites are the five loops in search-data.ts listed above plus the fixture helper in search.test.ts — add `updatedAt: true` to the four selects at search-data.ts:72/:78-84/:88-95/:99 and `updatedAt` to the org select at :58, and build the citation per row (origin TENURE_RECORD, assertion SOURCE, deepLink null: these are Tenure's own rows and the href is already an internal path). CONSUMERS TO CHECK AND FIX IN THE SAME CHANGE: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:271-276, apps/web/src/app/api/search/route.ts:22-28, modelSourceFor in apps/web/src/lib/relay/projection-policy.ts, and every fixture in search.test.ts / search-data.itest.ts / relay-prompt-safety.test.ts that builds a SearchDoc literal. (3) chat/route.ts:271-276 emits the citation with each source, and ai.ts:171-176's sourceBlock prefixes each numbered source with its state and observedAt so the model cannot present a STALE row as current, and states in the system message that a claim not traceable to a numbered source is an inference and must be labelled. MUTATION PROOF, on the producer not the helper: an itest against the running Postgres that ages a memory row's updatedAt past the stale window, POSTs /api/ai/chat, and asserts BOTH the returned source and the emitted prompt text carry STALE; then freeze `state` to 'CURRENT' inside the search-data.ts loop (the producer) and that test must red. A test that calls freshnessOf() directly proves nothing the moment the loop stops calling it.

title: No canonical Work Graph object exists — no ExternalObjectRef, SourceCitation, SyncObservation or Tombstone, and no §3.5 projection-state machine anywhere in the tree
why_open: Bible §3.2 (line 118) lists the canonical objects and §3.5 (line 215-241) fixes a projection state ladder DISCOVERED → AUTHORIZED → FETCH_PENDING → CURRENT → STALE → REFRESHING plus ten exceptional states (ACCESS_REVOKED, SOURCE_DELETED, SOURCE_MOVED, SOURCE_UNKNOWN, RETENTION_EXPIRED, LEGAL_HOLD, QUARANTINED, CLASSIFICATION_BLOCKED, INDEX_FAILED, MAPPING_CONFLICT). `ls packages/` returns audit, authorization, configuration, contracts, finops, identity, metadata, module-runtime, organization-model, payments, platform-config, provisioning, releases, workflow — there is no work-graph package. Grep for ExternalObjectRef / SyncObservation / Tombstone / ConnectionGrant across apps/web/src and packages/*/src returns exactly one hit and it is a disclaimer, not an implementation: apps/web/src/lib/connections/capability-resolution.ts:15-22 states in prose that '`Connection`, `ConnectionOpportunity`, `PendingActionIntent` and `ConnectionLaunchToken` (WRK-010-001 / WRK-030-002) exist in no package and no migration in this repository'. The one piece of §3 that HAS landed is §3.4's three data modes — apps/web/src/lib/relay/projection-policy.ts, cited as WRK-010-003 — which is the precedent for how the rest should land: one value type, one required field, one production caller. The state machine is unwritten: grep for STALE / SOURCE_DELETED / ACCESS_REVOKED across apps and packages returns nothing.
smallest_real_change: Do NOT declare sixty types nobody calls — that is the dead-code failure the bar forbids, and the ledger has already recorded it twice as the reason an item stayed open. Ship only the objects the citation path in WRK-070-003 consumes, and let that path be the caller: `ProjectionState` as a const tuple of the six normal plus ten exceptional states, `advance(state, event)` returning the next state or a typed refusal with SOURCE_DELETED / ACCESS_REVOKED / RETENTION_EXPIRED terminal (never returning to CURRENT), and `ExternalObjectRef` / `SyncObservation` / `Tombstone` with `parse*` functions that refuse a value missing tenant, provider or externalId. Wire it by having apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts build every row's citation through parseSourceCitation (which validates the state against the ladder), so the parser sits ON the request path rather than beside it. MUTATION PROOF through the route: drop `observedAt` from the object built in the search-data.ts loop and the /api/ai/chat route test must red with the parser's refusal — not a unit test calling advance() directly. Every remaining §3.2 object stays unwritten and the ledger entry says which ones and why, rather than claiming the section is done. THIS IS ONE EDIT WITH WRK-070-003 — same files, same agent; splitting them means two runs widening SearchDoc.

title: `confirmationToken` is accepted as any non-empty string — the human confirmation on the one door writes go through is bound to no plan, no digest, no actor, no expiry
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:624-637 is the whole of the confirmation gate: `if (tool.readOnly === false) { const token = proposal.args.confirmationToken; if (typeof token !== 'string' || token.trim().length === 0) refuse }`. The literal string 'y' passes. Bible §7.3 (line 484) is explicit: 'The confirmation is bound to a digest of the exact plan. A changed recipient, body, permission, attachment, target, or provider account invalidates prior approval.' Nothing computes a digest — grep for planDigest / ActionPlan / preview across apps/web/src and packages/*/src returns nothing — so the model can be confirmed for one plan and execute another, and §7.3's eleven-line preview and §7.4's receipt have no representation at all. What HAS landed is the risk classification: relay-tools.ts:93-107 declares ActionRiskClass READ|DRAFT|WRITE|BULK|EXTERNAL_SHARE|DELETE|PRIVILEGED (WRK-050-005) — a real vocabulary, but not §7.2's A0_OBSERVE..A5_PROTECTED_DOMAIN ladder, and crucially it is derived from the permission string, so nothing binds a class to a plan. The door is genuinely production-reached: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:245-261 calls invokeRelayTool on every request. The separate command bus is still dead — grep for '@/lib/commands' or 'commands/bus' across apps/web/src and tests returns only two comments saying so (packages/payments/src/gateway.ts:30, tests/architecture/payments-port-is-the-only-door.test.mjs:14), so apps/web/src/lib/commands/bus.ts:86 dispatch() still has zero production callers.
smallest_real_change: apps/web/src/lib/relay/action-plan.ts: `ActionPlan` carrying §7.3's fields that exist here today — acting identity, tenant, toolKey, target, recipients, body, notification flag, permission impact — and `planDigest(plan)`, a canonical key-order-independent SHA-256 (the same canonicalisation discipline apps/web/src/lib/provisioning/reconcile.ts already documents), plus `issueConfirmation(plan, secret, now, ttlMs)` returning an HMAC over digest+tenant+actor+expiry and `confirmationMatches(token, plan, context, now)` returning a typed refusal — PLAN_CHANGED | EXPIRED | WRONG_ACTOR | WRONG_TENANT | MALFORMED — never a boolean. Then replace relay-tools.ts:624-637 with that check, deriving the plan from the invocation's own resolved args so a caller cannot pass a plan that differs from what will run. The refusal already has somewhere to go: invokeRelayTool returns RefusedTool and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts surfaces it as toolRefusal. CONSUMERS CHECKED: invokeRelayTool has exactly two callers — apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:245 and apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.test.ts (:424, :434, :464, :470, :489 and neighbours); RelayInvocation/RefusedTool are consumed by chat/route.ts and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/ai-kill-switch.test.ts. ToolRegistration lives in packages/contracts and must NOT be widened — another cluster run owns that file — which is why the plan is derived at the door instead of declared on the registration. HONEST SCOPE: /api/ai/chat is read-only (SURFACE_TOOL_POLICY = 'read-only' at route.ts:151, EXECUTABLE_TOOLS = [search.corpus] at :154), so the writing branch has no live surface TODAY; the change is still real because invokeRelayTool is the single production door and the test drives it through authorizeRelayTools with a writing registration exactly as relay-tools.test.ts already does. MUTATION PROOF: build a plan, issue its confirmation, change one recipient, invoke — assert PLAN_CHANGED; then mutate the producer by dropping `recipients` from the digest input inside action-plan.ts's canonicaliser and that test must red. Preview, receipt, compensation and reconciliation remain FAIL and the ledger must say so, naming apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma (no IdempotencyRecord model; the only idempotencyKey is ApprovalRequest's) and packages/contracts as the files that would have to move for the rest.

title: No connection class exists, so class escalation cannot be prohibited — a webhook-only grant and an org-wide app identity are the same thing to every decision in the tree
why_open: Bible §4.1 (lines 248-259) names eight classes — USER_DELEGATED, ADMIN_DELEGATED, APPLICATION_ORG_WIDE, BOT_OR_APP_INSTALLATION, SERVICE_ACCOUNT, WEBHOOK_ONLY, FILE_OR_FEED, PERSONAL_PRODUCTIVITY — and requires that 'Connection class, provider consent, and Tenure authorization must all agree'. Grep for USER_DELEGATED / APPLICATION_ORG_WIDE / WEBHOOK_ONLY / connectionClass across apps/web/src and packages/*/src returns nothing outside the Bible. The one live authorization surface a connector would pass through is authorizeRegistrations / authorizeRelayTools in apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts, and it decides on three Tenure-side facts only: the surface ceiling (`allow`), `tool.requiredPermission` through decideCheck, and the owning-domain policy for BULK/EXTERNAL_SHARE/DELETE/PRIVILEGED (relay-tools.ts:380-420). Nothing in the decision represents what the PROVIDER consented to, so there is no place in this codebase where the sentence 'this connection may not do that' can currently be written. packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts:83 has `CapabilityDirection` (read|write|bidirectional) and packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts declares 24 packs — but that is Tenure's side, it is engine-only (tests/security/cell-independence.test.mjs forbids apps/web importing @tenure/provisioning), and no row carries a connection class.
smallest_real_change: apps/web/src/lib/relay/connection-class.ts declares the eight classes as a const tuple and, for each, the maximum ActionRiskClass it may reach (relay-tools.ts:93-107 already exports that vocabulary) plus whether it may serve tenant-wide use (PERSONAL_PRODUCTIVITY may not, WEBHOOK_ONLY reaches nothing above READ). Export `refuseEscalation(granted, requested)` returning { ok: true } or a refusal naming BOTH classes and the ceiling — never a boolean, so the reason survives to the person. Make it live at the one real decision point: carry the class on the cell-readable capability record (extend the provider-review record in packages/platform-config, which apps/web already imports at api/ai/chat/route.ts:298 — do NOT reach for @tenure/provisioning, tests/security/cell-independence.test.mjs:20-27 refuses it and lists its single exemption), and have authorizeRegistrations push a RefusedTool when a tool's derived riskClass exceeds the class its capability is offered under. MUTATION PROOF through the route: register a probe capability at WEBHOOK_ONLY whose tool derives WRITE, POST /api/ai/chat, assert the response's toolRefusal names the escalation and both class names; then delete the class check from relay-tools.ts (the producer) and that route test must red. Do not call refuseEscalation() from the test. CONSUMERS CHECKED: RelayToolset / OfferedTool / RefusedTool are consumed only by apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:236-261 and :399-424, apps/web/src/app/api/ai/ai-kill-switch.test.ts:559, and apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.test.ts. ToolRegistration in packages/contracts must NOT be widened — another cluster run owns it. SAME FILE AREA AS WRK-050-002 and WRK-GATE-020: give all three to one agent.

title: Tenant and purpose authority are enforced; resource and direction authority are not represented at all, so a granted connection has no ceiling to exceed
why_open: The gate asks that connections cannot exceed granted identity, resource, direction, purpose or tenant authority. Three of the five are genuinely enforced and should not be re-done: tenant and identity (apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:610-622 refuses a proposal naming tenantId/institutionId/connectionId/accountId/apiKey/onBehalfOf and :659-666 stamps them from the validated TenantContext), and purpose (apps/web/src/lib/search-data.ts:213-224 splits loadSearchCorpus from loadInteractiveSearchCorpus so the vendor-bound read and the render-bound read are different calls, cited as WRK-070-002). The other two do not exist. DIRECTION: `CapabilityDirection` is declared in packages/provisioning/src/connector-capability.ts:83 and every pack in packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts carries one, but that package is engine-only and unreachable from the cell (tests/security/cell-independence.test.mjs), and nothing on the request path reads a direction — a read grant and a write grant are indistinguishable at apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.ts:624-637. RESOURCE: Bible §4.2 'Resource selectors' (line 261) has no representation anywhere; grep for resourceSelector / includeExclude / selectedContainers across apps and packages returns nothing, and RelayInvocationLimits (relay-tools.ts:~488-505) bounds recipients and tool keys but names no container, mailbox, folder or channel. The §4.1 sentence 'Never turn a user token into organization-wide data access by iterating over discoverable resources' is therefore unenforceable by construction.
smallest_real_change: Extend RelayInvocationLimits with a REQUIRED `grantedDirection: 'read' | 'write' | 'bidirectional'` and a REQUIRED `selectedResources: readonly string[]` (empty meaning none, which refuses every resource argument — the same honest shape `allowedRecipients: []` already uses at api/ai/chat/route.ts:259). Required, not optional: an optional field the one caller forgets compiles, passes every unit test that builds its own fixture, and fails in production — the exact failure mode this session recorded twice. Then in invokeRelayTool refuse a writing tool under a read-only grant, and refuse any argument naming a container/folder/mailbox/channel outside `selectedResources`, both as RefusedTool with the granted and requested values named. CONSUMERS TO FIX IN THE SAME CHANGE — every construction site of RelayInvocationLimits: apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:255-260 (the one production caller; it passes grantedDirection 'read' and selectedResources [] truthfully) and apps/web/src/lib/relay-tools.test.ts's `limits` fixture used at :424, :434, :464, :470, :489. MUTATION PROOF on the producer: POST /api/ai/chat with a proposal naming a folder argument and assert the refusal names the empty selection; then have route.ts pass a wildcard selection and the test must red. Record honestly in the ledger that identity/tenant/purpose were already enforced and by which lines, so the entry is not a claim that this run built all five. SAME FILE AS WRK-020-001 and WRK-050-002 — one agent, one pass over relay-tools.ts.

title: A Microsoft Graph two-way calendar sync is claimed in code and to the user's face, backed by a dead process-global provider slot with zero callers and no certification record
why_open: apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:10-12 states 'When Microsoft Graph credentials are provided, a real two-way GraphCalendarSync implements the CalendarSyncProvider below and drops in with no change to callers', and apps/web/src/components/CalendarSubscribe.tsx:83-84 repeats it to the user: 'Two-way sync (edits made in Outlook flowing back into Tenure) turns on once your institution connects Microsoft 365.' No connector exists — grep for graph.microsoft.com across apps/web/src returns nothing but that comment. The seam it points at is dead: `calendarSync()` (calendar-sync.ts:29-31) and `setCalendarSyncProvider()` (:32-34) have zero callers anywhere; the only imports of the module are `calendarToken` at apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/page.tsx:9 and `verifyCalendarToken, eventsToICS` at apps/web/src/app/api/calendar/ics/[token]/route.ts:2. So 'drops in with no change to callers' is true only because there are no callers. And the slot is a module-level mutable singleton (`let provider` at :28) with no tenant in its key — one institution's connector, once set, would serve every institution in the process, which is WRK-GATE-020's tenant authority violated by construction before a provider is ever written. Meanwhile the machinery to say this honestly already exists and is unused here: packages/platform-config/src/provider-review.ts:109-200 exports `providerActivation(requestedScopes, review, now)` with the four verdicts, and apps/web/src/app/api/ai/chat/route.ts:298-302 already gates the one real outbound integration on it. Nothing equivalent guards the calendar claim, and packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts:131-141 records microsoft.outlook-mail and google.gmail at PLANNED — engine-side, invisible to the cell.
smallest_real_change: (1) Delete the dead seam — the CalendarSyncProvider interface, IcsFeedSync, the `let provider` singleton, calendarSync() and setCalendarSyncProvider() (calendar-sync.ts:15-34) — and rewrite the module comment to claim only what ships, a per-user ICS feed. Grep before and after: nothing imports them, so the deletion breaks no caller. (2) packages/platform-config/src/provider-review.ts gains GRAPH_CALENDAR_SCOPES (['microsoft:Calendars.ReadWrite']) and GRAPH_CALENDAR_REVIEW = undefined-or-NOT_SUBMITTED, written in the same honest voice as RELAY_ANTHROPIC_REVIEW at :180-200 — no review has been submitted, and a credential is not a review. (3) The sentence a user reads becomes a lookup: apps/web/src/components/CalendarSubscribe.tsx:83-84 and apps/web/src/app/(app)/calendar/page.tsx:223 render from `providerActivation(GRAPH_CALENDAR_SCOPES, GRAPH_CALENDAR_REVIEW, now)`, which today returns provider-review-missing, so the copy says the feed is one-way and does not promise a future. platform-config is cell-safe by design (its own header at provider-review.ts:11-20 says so) — do NOT import @tenure/provisioning from apps/web; tests/security/cell-independence.test.mjs refuses it with exactly one listed exemption. (4) tests/architecture/no-uncertified-provider-claims.test.mjs, built in the shape of tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs (git ls-files, comments not stripped — the false claim here IS a comment), fails when a provider brand name appears next to a capability verb (sync/send/create/two-way/flowing back) in apps/web/src unless the same file reads providerActivation, with each exemption stating why. MUTATION PROOF: flip GRAPH_CALENDAR_REVIEW to APPROVED covering the scopes and the CalendarSubscribe test asserting the rendered sentence must change; flip it back. Then re-add the bare 'two-way sync turns on once...' sentence and the architecture guard must red. NOTE: tests/architecture/forbidden-clients.test.mjs is modified in the working tree by a concurrent run — do not edit it, add a new file. apps/web/src/components/CalendarSubscribe.tsx is clean (only shell/ShellHeader.tsx and ui/PageHeader.tsx are dirty under components/).

title: `PendingActionIntent` is a React prop that is thrown away, `ConnectionOpportunity` does not exist, and there is no launch token of any kind — single-use or otherwise
why_open: Bible §5.2 (line 317) requires a server-side ConnectionOpportunity carrying thirteen named facts (capability and action, preferred/alternative certified packs, tenant/environment/seat/legal-entity/region/plan, connection class and required installer authority, minimal scopes, resource-selection model, data-use-retention summary, risk class and required approval, the PendingActionIntent reference, expiration and one-time-use policy, safe return location), and §5.3 (line 335) requires an opaque token that is 'signed, audience-bound, tenant-bound, user/session-bound when applicable, short-lived, single-use, nonce-protected, and redeemable only after current Tenure authentication'. None of it exists, and the code says so in its own words: apps/web/src/lib/connections/capability-resolution.ts:15-22 states that Connection, ConnectionOpportunity, PendingActionIntent and ConnectionLaunchToken 'exist in no package and no migration in this repository'. What does exist is the shape of the hole: apps/web/src/components/connections/MissingConnectionCard.tsx:27-33 takes `pendingIntent` and its own comment says 'Never persisted anywhere — this is component state passed straight back out', and apps/web/src/components/ai/TenureAIPanel.tsx:305-313 passes the user's question into it. So the promise on the card — 'Kept for when this connects' (MissingConnectionCard.tsx:59-62) — survives exactly as long as the React tree does: a refresh, a sign-in redirect or a cross-device return loses it, which is precisely what §5.3 step 2 ('send to Tenure sign-in/sign-up and preserve only the opaque pending intent') exists to prevent. The nearest token machinery in the tree is the calendar feed token at apps/web/src/lib/calendar-sync.ts:41-58 — deliberately STABLE per user and infinitely replayable, the opposite of single-use, and a good thing to point at as what this must not copy.
smallest_real_change: SCHEMA NOTICE — this item needs one new Prisma model and a migration in apps/web/prisma/schema.prisma; the orchestrator asked that this be stated, and no other item in this survey touches the schema. (1) A `ConnectionLaunchToken` model: id, tenant (institutionId), userId, capabilityKey, opaque tokenHash (store the hash, never the token), pendingIntent TEXT (the user's own words, which is why it is a column and not a URL parameter — §5.2 'Do not store raw user prompt content in the redirect URL'), returnPath, expiresAt, consumedAt, nonce. Single-use is the `consumedAt` write inside the same transaction that reads the row, not a check-then-write. (2) apps/web/src/lib/connections/pending-intent.ts: `openConnectionOpportunity(scope, capability, intent)` minting the token and returning the opaque value, and `redeemConnectionLaunchToken(token, session)` returning the intent or a typed refusal — EXPIRED | ALREADY_CONSUMED | WRONG_TENANT | WRONG_USER | UNKNOWN. Both run inside the existing tenant scope; note REVIEW-FINDINGS §16 is closed and `withTransactionGuard` (apps/web/src/lib/db.ts:137) already wraps $transaction, so do not add a second guard, and keep any redirect outside the scope body. (3) The production caller is the card that already promises resumption: MissingConnectionCard's onConnect path and TenureAIPanel.tsx:305-313 mint the opportunity server-side and carry the opaque token, so the kept question survives a sign-in round trip instead of a re-render. MUTATION PROOF against the running Postgres (docker ps shows it up): an itest that mints one token, redeems it, asserts the intent comes back, redeems the SAME token again and asserts ALREADY_CONSUMED with exactly one consumedAt write; then mutate the producer — make redeem read the row without writing consumedAt — and the second assertion must red. A second test redeems under a different userId and asserts WRONG_USER. Scope the fixture teardown to the ids it created: this session reddened two unrelated suites when a fixture deleted the seeded pilot institution. The rest of §5.2's thirteen fields (certified alternative packs, region, plan, installer authority) stay unwritten until there is a certified pack to name, and the ledger entry says which ones and why.

title: The Connection Center is one settings card that collapses four different outcomes into the words "Not connected", and §13.3's status vocabulary appears nowhere
why_open: Bible §13.1 (line 784) names nine tenant-facing surfaces and §13.3 (line 809) fixes the exact status words a user may be shown — Ready / Needs your attention / Waiting for admin / Limited / Temporarily unavailable / Disconnected / Not available yet — with 'Not available yet' explicitly meaning 'connector/capability not certified; no fake connect action'. What ships is one card: apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings/page.tsx:326-364 renders three hard-declared capabilities (ai.model, documents.storage, calendar.feed at :52-92) and at :357-358 prints `resolved.outcome === 'CONNECTED' ? 'Connected' : 'Not connected'`. That single ternary collapses NEEDS_USER_CONNECT, NEEDS_ADMIN, NOT_CERTIFIED and UNAVAILABLE into one phrase — so a capability the platform has not certified, one waiting on an administrator, and one the user could connect from their own seat all read identically, which is the exact confusion §13.3 exists to remove. The page also computes `resolved.action` (capability-resolution.ts:63-71 returns one control per outcome) and then never renders it, so the 'connect / ask an administrator / disconnect' path that the resolver decides has no surface on the Connection Center at all — only the AI panel's card (apps/web/src/components/connections/MissingConnectionCard.tsx:66-86) renders a control. None of §13.1's other surfaces exist: grep for 'last used', health, receipts, requests, retention across apps/web/src/app/(app)/settings returns nothing, and there is no /connections route. The ledger has WRK-110-001 FAIL at docs/implementation/universal-work-graph-execution-ledger.md:621-623.
smallest_real_change: Do not build nine surfaces nobody asked for. Make the two that exist tell the truth. (1) capability-resolution.ts gains `statusWord(outcome): 'Ready' | 'Needs your attention' | 'Waiting for admin' | 'Limited' | 'Temporarily unavailable' | 'Disconnected' | 'Not available yet'` — a total mapping over ConnectionOutcome so a new outcome is a compile error rather than a silent fall-through to a default, which is how the current ternary went wrong. (2) settings/page.tsx:357-358 renders that word instead of the ternary, and renders `resolved.action` as the one control the resolver allows (it already computes it and discards it) — 'Ask an administrator' for NEEDS_ADMIN, nothing at all for NOT_CERTIFIED, which is §13.3's 'no fake connect action' made structural. (3) MissingConnectionCard.tsx renders the same word so the panel and the settings page cannot drift. MUTATION PROOF on the producer, through the rendered page: a Playwright assertion (apps/web runs both suites locally in minutes) that with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY unset the ai.model row reads 'Waiting for admin' and NOT 'Not connected', and that a capability declared `certified: false` reads 'Not available yet' AND renders no button; then mutate settings/page.tsx back to the boolean ternary and both must red. Do not assert by calling statusWord() — the defect is that the page discards what the resolver returns. NEIGHBOUR: this is the same two files as WRK-030-002 (MissingConnectionCard, TenureAIPanel, capability-resolution) — one agent. Components under apps/web/src/components are clean except shell/ShellHeader.tsx and ui/PageHeader.tsx, which a concurrent run holds; do not touch those two.

title: Raw-body verification, replay defence and durable acceptance exist for exactly one provider and are locked inside @tenure/payments; the workspace-connector inbound edge does not exist
why_open: The requirement covers events ARRIVING from a provider. One inbound endpoint now exists and it is good: apps/web/src/app/api/payments/provider-events/route.ts:75-83 reads `request.text()` before anything parses it, verifies against an ARRAY of secrets for rotation overlap, checks a pinned api_version, parses against the declared field set, dedupes at :146 and persists a receipt at :153-163. But every piece of it is bound to one provider: `verifySignature`, `dedupe`, `parseProviderEvent`, `PROVIDER` and `PROVIDER_API_VERSION` are imported from @tenure/payments and the header is read as `stripe-signature` at :76, so nothing here is reachable by a workspace connector. `find apps/web/src/app/api -name route.ts` lists 25 routes and that is the only inbound one — there is no connector event endpoint of any kind. apps/web/src/lib/http/ contains only internal-headers.ts. Subscription verification and renewal (Graph change-notification lifecycle, Google watch expiry) and catch-up have no representation at all: grep for subscriptionId / watch / renewal across apps/web/src returns nothing. The honest complication, which must be stated rather than worked around: packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts declares all 24 packs at PLANNED, so an inbound connector route would today refuse every provider — and a route that refuses everything is close to the declaration-with-no-caller this bar forbids.
smallest_real_change: The defensible change is extraction, not a speculative endpoint. Move the provider-agnostic half into apps/web/src/lib/http/signed-delivery.ts — edge-safe, no next/*, no @/lib/db, matching the discipline internal-headers.ts already states: `verifySignedDelivery({ rawBody, signatureHeader, secrets, now, toleranceMs })` recomputing an HMAC over the EXACT bytes, comparing with timingSafeEqual over equal-length digests, refusing outside the tolerance window, returning a typed refusal (BAD_SIGNATURE | OUTSIDE_WINDOW | MALFORMED_HEADER) and the matched secret index — never a boolean. Then have apps/web/src/app/api/payments/provider-events/route.ts call it, so there is ONE implementation with a live caller rather than a second copy waiting for a connector. The scheme parsing that is genuinely Stripe-shaped (the `t=`/`v1=` header grammar) stays behind a `scheme` parameter with the Stripe grammar as the first registered one. MUTATION PROOF, driving the ROUTE not the helper: POST a body whose signature was computed over a re-ordered JSON re-serialisation and assert 400 — this is the mutation that catches verifying over the parsed object; POST a delivery signed 10 minutes ago and assert the window refusal; then mutate the producer by having the route JSON.parse and re-stringify before verifying, and the first test must red. HONEST SCOPE, to be recorded rather than claimed: this closes raw-body verification and replay window as reusable behaviour and leaves WRK-060-002 FAIL for subscription verification/renewal and catch-up, which have no provider to renew against — packages/provisioning/src/provider-packs.ts has every workspace pack at PLANNED. Do not invent a connector event route to make the item look closed. CONFLICT NOTE: this touches packages/payments only if the extraction moves code out of it; if the PAY cluster run is live on that package, extract into apps/web/src/lib/http and have the route import from there, leaving @tenure/payments untouched.
